simulations.scenario: Take a lesson at the K-12 hall, carry it to the Trade School, and bring it back. A lesson taught twice is a lesson learned.

scoring.notes: Mirrors the in-world quest 'First Lesson'. Four steps, in order.
scoring.pass: All steps in order, every check passed. Practice score only — it certifies nothing.

steps.action: Talk to the K-12 Teacher and take the lesson.
steps.check: Lesson received; the teacher's three steps noted.
steps.if_wrong: Ask again — the lesson starts with the teacher.

steps.action: Collect the Lesson Spark at the K-12 hall.
steps.if_wrong: The spark is at the K-12 hall, door-side. Look again.

steps.action: Visit the Trade School hall and show the lesson to the Trade School Instructor.
steps.check: Instructor shown the lesson; their response noted.
steps.if_wrong: The Trade School hall is the next hall along. Go there, don't guess.

steps.action: Report back to the K-12 Teacher: what the lesson became at the Trade School.
steps.check: Report given in your own words.
steps.if_wrong: A report in the teacher's words is not a report. Use your own.

simulations.title: First Lesson, Taught Twice

simulations.label: SIMULATION — practice only. Not a licence, not a certification, not a credential, not a diagnosis, not advice for any real person, site or deal.
simulations.scenario: Taste three halls — Trade School, Making Repair & Reuse, Robotics OS — and choose one to go deeper on.

scoring.notes: A taster, not a trade. Choosing is the point.
scoring.pass: All steps in order, every check passed. Practice score only — it certifies nothing.

steps.action: At the Trade School, name one skill the hall teaches and one tool it uses.
steps.check: One skill and one tool named.
steps.if_wrong: Name both. A skill without a tool is a wish.

steps.action: At Making, Repair & Reuse, pick up a practice piece and name what is wrong with it.
steps.check: The fault named before any fix is attempted.
steps.if_wrong: Fixing before naming the fault is guessing. Name it first.

steps.action: At Robotics OS, read the control console rules before touching the arm stand.
steps.check: Console rules read; arm untouched until the rules are known.
steps.if_wrong: The arm is practice hardware with simulated power. Rules first, always.

steps.action: Choose one hall to go deeper on, and say why in one sentence.
steps.check: One hall chosen, one reason given.
steps.if_wrong: Choosing is the lesson. Pick one.

simulations.title: Trade Path Taster

sources: Anchor: lat 45.483127839031816, lon 18.572453605834877. Status anchored = real-world anchor coordinate exists; rp1 null, NOT live on RP1.
Fabric: 26 nodes total (scene root + 25 top-level packs); 26 distinct GLB refs, all unhosted — see missing_models.

Buildings = all 25 real top-level pack nodes (K–12, Trade School, Future-Work, Regional, Civic & Leadership, Health & Community, Language Culture & Communication, Empathy & Emotional Intelligence, Community & Relationship Practice, Preventive Health, Basic Life Skills, Water Land & Climate, Care Across a Life, Making Repair & Reuse, Housing & Tenancy, Money Benefits & Entitlements, Reentry & Recovery, Neighbourhood Safety & Civic Voice, Corporate OS, Science OS, Robotics OS, Global Health OS, Multilateral OS, Sapient OS, Non-Profit Practice). Districts = 5 of those nodes used as district anchors (design choice).
NPCs: the Cognition fabric has no 'Agent · ...' nodes; NPC roles are named after real fabric pack nodes and all dialogue is original game dialogue, never attributed to a real person.
Biome 'campus' is a design choice for this interpretation.
Agent companions are game characters representing the real Virtuals agents (agents.json); their live instances are offline — not live connections.

stations.content: Per the Cognition.X wiki (data model, README): each track contains 10 themes, each theme taught at 5 grade bands — K-2 and 3-5 at Explorer level, 6-8 at Builder, 9-10 at Practitioner, 11-12 at Lead — so a track is 50 blocks and one credential. Legacy packs (K-12, Trade School, grade-banded community packs) predate that shape and are kept verbatim. Block/pack totals conflict between repos (6,750/25 in agi-corp-worlds vs 17,450/47 in the Cognition.X repo) — neither figure is quoted as settled.
stations.name: Track structure — 10 themes, 5 grade bands, 50 blocks
stations.summary: How a Cognition.X track is built.

stations.content: Per the Cognition.X wiki: Simulation Studio — 18 scenarios, one engine, six apps; 'simulation is not certification' (docs/SIMULATION.md). Standards mapping and transfer-check rubrics are 'intended alignment, never certification' (docs/STANDARDS.md). The simulations in this world follow the same rule.
stations.name: Simulation Studio — 18 scenarios

stations.content: Per the Cognition.X wiki, the Trades Network app holds 222 union & trade entries across 6 regions. The six apps are Education OS, Flow Hub, Louisiana (64 parish dashboards), Trades Network, States (all 50 states), and Platform. This hall is a learning space about that network, not the network itself.
stations.name: Trades Network — 222 union & trade entries
stations.summary: The Trades Network app, in one station.

stations.content: Per the Cognition.X wiki: credential records use a native format plus an Open Badges 3.0 envelope, verified with node tools/verify_record.js (docs/CREDENTIALS.md). Nothing earned in this world is a credential — the sparks and relics here are game collectibles only.
stations.name: Credential records — Open Badges 3.0
stations.summary: How a Cognition.X credential record is verified.
